There was a rumor that the music room was haunted, but by what, no one can say. Some people claimed to hear wailing and scratching coming from inside the walls, while others spoke of a honking noise coming from the instruments themselves. Mydei didn’t have the luxury of choosing a non-haunted music room, so it didn’t matter what poltergeist made its home there as long as it let Mydei work in peace.

Mydei underestimated how much of a problem it would be. How was anyone going to get work done with so much weeping and sobbing going on?

With a frustrated groan, Mydei got up from the piano and tracked where the sobs were coming from. The sound led him to the corner where they dump the extra equipment, and with a strong kick, Mydei displaced a pile of music stands to reveal the resentful spirit taking its revenge on him.

Oh, it’s the gloomy kid. Figures. Maybe he’d stop being gloomy if people called him something else, but it’s not like Mydei could figure out a better name for him. The boy looked up at Mydei with his teary eyes wide with shock, a line of snot smeared all the way up to his cheek. Mydei felt bad for him, but the kid also needed to know that this was not the best place for privacy.

“Stop crying,” Mydei said. “You’re not the only one who needs this room.”

The boy sniffled. Drat, that’s not what Mydei wanted. He tried desperately to think of a way to calm the kid down, but he couldn’t muster any comforting words fast enough. Mydei gave up and braced himself for more bawling, only to be shot a scorching glare.

“Like you were doing anything important,” the boy spat out.

That took Mydei aback, and any patience he had quickly evaporated.

“I’m writing a song for my mom,” he said bluntly. “She’s in the hospital because her lungs are failing.”

The boy blinked at him. If he wanted a reason to cry, then by hook or by crook Mydei would give him one.

“Well, um, your song is stupid,” the boy countered. “Who wants to hear a sad song when they’re already sad?”

Mydei could pummel this kid, but he had a point.

Fist clenched, Mydei forced himself to leave this lost cause to his tears. He stomped over to the piano, where he would sit unmoving in silence for the better part of an hour. The other boy sniffed and rustled around in the meantime, but it was nowhere as distracting as his previous waterworks.

Eventually the boy got up. He was padding towards the exit when a clumsy melody began to play from the piano. It sounded childish, probably due to who was composing it, but it was also kind in an awkward sort of way. Every note resolved predictably, like it endeavored so hard to be reassuring that it looped back to being patronizingly trite.

When it ended, Mydei turned to the boy with his chin jutted out in challenge. The boy huffed.

“I liked the last song better,” the boy said.

Mydei frowned. “You said it was bad.”

“No I said it was sad! All you had to do was make it go up at the end.”

“Go up what?”

“I don’t know. You’re the piano player.”

These were terrible instructions. Nevertheless, Mydei replayed the song he’d been busy composing prior, but with the ending revised so it went ‘up’.

The boy hummed in thought. “Now it sounds kinda weird.”

“Yeah, because you told me to make it weird.”

“You have to make the rest match too,” the boy said matter-of-factly as he walked over to where Mydei sat. “Like keep it moving the same, but have all the last parts go up.”

“So stupid.”

The boy pouted. “Play it and see if it’s stupid!”

Mydei obeyed. He fiddled with the notes until they sounded coherently ‘up’, and eventually got to somewhere far more pleasing than either of them expected.

“It’s okay,” Mydei said. “But now it doesn’t go with the rest of the song.”

“How does it go?” The boy asked, plopping himself down on the stool beside Mydei. “I bet you can just do the same thing again.”

“I can’t because it sounds like this.” Mydei played him another sample.

“Hmm, it kinda sounds like a song that my uncle likes. Try making it sound like bup-bup-bup.”

“I don’t want to rip off a song.”

“It’s called being inspired.”

“… It doesn’t sound bad. It might sound better over here though.”

“Wow. You can actually play the piano!”

“What do you think I’ve been doing, butthead?”

“For your information, my name is Phainon. Now, let me hear everything we’ve got so far!”

Mydei’s breath fogs over in the evening air.

Winters in Castrum Kremnos almost never see snow, so Mydei had to take a look for himself when he caught wind of the weather report. He got outside too late to watch it happen, but there it is, a thin blanket of white draped over the streets of his hometown. With only a handful of people out at this late hour, the snow sits pristine and undisturbed, inviting in its perfection. It shimmers delicately under the lamp lights, tiny crystals mirroring the myriad constellations twinkling in the night sky.

A noise alerts Mydei of someone approaching from behind. Mydei turns to see a head of yellow bobbing towards him, fine snow crunching beneath the man’s boots.

“There you are,” Phainon says with an exasperated sigh. “You should really put on more layers before you step out in this weather.”

Mydei scoffs. His leather jacket is already doing a good job of keeping him well-heated. Besides- “I wanted to cool down.”

The bar was too stuffy, with its low ceilings and its legion of regulars. Mydei found it perfect for the weather, so warm and snug and full of life. Their tiny stage sat close to the drinking and dancing, allowing Mydei to revel in the warmth of the crowd’s cavorting bodies while he and Phainon sustained them with music. It may have gotten too much by the end of the set, but it’s an easy fix with nights like this.

“Yeah well, there are better ways to get some air,” Phainon grumbles, unwinding the scarf around his neck. “Did you even try to wipe your sweat off at all?”

“I won’t get sick,” Mydei swears.

Mydei may run hotter than the average person, but that doesn’t make him any better with the cold. Phainon feels like the only person who’s aware of his low tolerance, and he almost looks forward to when Mydei is reminded of it in the morning, when he’s bundled up and shivering in Phainon’s arms.

But Phainon hates the thought of Mydei’s discomfort even more. So he wraps his scarf around Mydei’s head and takes care to not snag on his

piercing when he covers his ears.

Mydei lets out a Scrooge-like harrumph, appropriate for the time of year. His cheeks redden too, and out of kindness Phainon pretends it was the cold snap that did it.

“Are you implying that you can handle this weather better than me?” Mydei questions.

Phainon can’t imply something that’s already fact. “Unlike you, I checked the weather app before leaving the motel,” Phainon says, pulling out heat packs and hand warmers from his coat.

Mydei sneers at Phainon’s superior foresight. “I’ve got a better way of keeping warm.”

“What c- Oh, you asshole.”

Before Phainon could ask, Mydei had taken off running, knowing full well that Phainon’s instincts would have him following suit without thinking twice. A part of Phainon’s brain dutifully stays behind reciting the logistics of their equipment - whether it’s back in their van and in good condition - while another curses Mydei for securing an unfair head start.

The rest of Phainon waxes poetic about the man in front of him, about his long strides and his composed running form. Mydei’s jacket flies up in the wind and exposes his exquisite back, his muscles flexing with each powerful step. He laughs haughtily to provoke Phainon and then he glances back because he can’t help himself. Yes, Phainon is still running after him, and yes, Phainon is taking care not to slip on the ice.

Even Mydei’s deviousness is a thing of beauty. Years of knowing each other, and Mydei still finds a way to keep Phainon on his toes. He can still make Phainon’s heart somersault at his behest, the little lion tamer that he is. As Mydei runs under the colonnade of streetlights, blinking in and out of sight each time he treads into the dark, Phainon’s heart squeezes with the loss and rejoices when he returns. Mydei has made him into a fool. A happy, easily-indulged fool.

Suddenly, Mydei stops running. That’s the advantage of being the one to start the race, you also get to be the one who decides when it’s finished. Phainon reaches him ready to complain when a freezing droplet lands upon his nose and stops him dead in his tracks.

A flurry of snow falls from the sky in gentle waves. The snowflakes take their time coming down, appearing to float in the air like in one of those novelty globes occupying Phainon and Mydei’s shelves. It’s even colder now, definitely beyond what Mydei can handle, and yet he’s in no hurry to seek shelter.

Beside him, Phainon runs a hand through his hair to shake off the frost. The hair dye is convenient, because otherwise Mydei might have lost him in the snow. Phainon is currently working through the hair dye section of their supermarket from lightest to darkest, and right now he’s touting a spiky bright yellow hairdo. Not yellow as in blond, but yellow as in neon. It’s a shade of highlighter that would have been prohibited at school, but Phainon is way too pleased with how it looks. He’s obviously looking forward to get to the more outrageous colors, and Mydei had been too, until he realized that Phainon is devilishly handsome in everything. It’s really difficult to poke fun at his partner sometimes, but never say Mydei never tries.

Aglaea dreads it though, and she makes no secret of it. As the head of a brand new talent agency, Aglaea is under tremendous pressure to turn a profit soon, and it would help if her artists aren’t a perm away from a perpetual clown wig. Before he could get within a meter of a salon, Aglaea forced Phainon to present his case formally, with full presentations and case studies to support his rhetoric. Needless to say Phainon won, and now he walks around looking like a warning to incoming drivers. Mydei suspects Aglaea had planned to give in anyway, because she began consulting Phainon about their clients after that incident. Whatever she plans with him seems to be years or decades into the future, and when Mydei pesters him about it, Phainon bashfully smiles and brings up the classes he’s been taking.

“You sure like snow, huh?” Phainon says.

Mydei side-eyes him. He’s not giving into Phainon’s trap that quickly.

Instead Mydei says, “That volcano I told you about-“

“-The Great Forge,” Phainon quickly completes, always eager to prove his excellent listening skills.

“…Yes, that. If we’re lucky we’ll get to see it on the way to Janusopolis,” Mydei tells him. “And if we’re unlucky we’ll get an example of what makes it so great.”

Mydei holds out his hand to catch the falling snow. “The Forge’s ashfall is as magnificent as it is destructive,” Mydei says. “This snow is probably the closest I’ll get to seeing it again.”

Phainon looks up at the sky, trying to picture what Mydei had described. He imagines it would appear as dark, with volcanic smog rising up to blot out the sun. Nowhere as serene, probably, but maybe as wondrous.

“Are you sure you don’t want to write the lyrics for our next album?” Phainon asks Mydei.

Mydei grimaces.

“Maybe you can start with a chorus,” Phainon suggests. “Help me like I help you.”

“You talk plenty for the both of us,” Mydei says. “But who knows what we’ll write next.”

Phainon and Mydei’s last album was country rock. The one before that was ska jazz, and further back was a little electric bossa nova. There’s been hits and misses, Phainon won’t deny that, and his old following had gone through a mass exodus by the time that first album hit the shelves. It’s hard, sometimes even harder than Phainon thought it would be. It took time for Phainon to detach himself from numbers and online reviews, too readily gripped by frustration and woe. If Mydei hadn’t been there to defy him, to push him and to uplift him, Phainon might have fallen back to his old ways.

If he did, then Phainon wouldn’t have gotten to hear all the songs they’ve made together. From the silly jokes to the protest songs, from the heartbreaking ballads to the awful, awful cheesy love poems… Though impressions may vary, each song is near and dear to Phainon’s heart. Every new endeavor is a brand new lesson or a memory shared with the love of his life, and the more they fill out their strange eclectic discography, the more Phainon is assured that he’s made the right decision. He’d be stupid to trade it for an empty home and a fear of time ticking down.

The broadness of their music also gives them the opportunity to tour the country, visiting venues both big and small to play to people from different walks of life. Phainon did more traveling at the height of his popularity, but he's never really immersed himself in what Amphoreus had to offer. Cyrene’s travel guides always urged readers to see it for themselves, yet Phainon only understood once he lost a game of chess in a seedy Styxian pub. Their music has even taken them to places outside Amphoreus. One of Phainon’s old collaborators, an overseas idol, sampled Phainon and Mydei’s work for one of their singles. The exposure that gave them allowed Phainon and Mydei to play at a handful festivals abroad, and though the experience was exhilarating, Amphoreus remains their most effective muse. They decided then to take a realistic approach for their career: conquer Amphoreus first before moving on to the rest of the world.

Mydei sneezes. It seems the heat from the exercise has worn off.

Phainon clicks his tongue. “What did I say?”

“I’m adapting,” Mydei excuses himself, as if Phainon can’t hear his teeth chattering in his mouth.

“Sure,” Phainon says with a shake of his head. “Now let me show you the best way to warm up.”

Phainon places his palms on Mydei’s cheeks, still toasty from all the warming agents in his pockets. With an imperceptible sigh, Mydei closes his eyes and nuzzles his face against Phainon’s touch. Once again, Phainon’s heart flips over in his chest and lands with an ungraceful thump.

As the heat slowly thaws his face, Mydei’s eyes flutter open once more. “Is that the best you can do?” He challenges.

Phainon chuckles, his smile lines out in full force. “Of course not.”

Dawn breaks on the horizon, its cold light spilling onto Castrum Kremnos. Phainon kisses Mydei on the open street, demonstrating the proper way to keep someone warm. Ever the good student, Mydei studies it well and puts it to use as soon as he can, for it would be a shame if Phainon himself were to fall ill in his place. Phainon, of course, would have it no other way.

With one last laugh, the two break apart to head back to their van together. Despite being a new day, the winter sun takes its time to properly rise. But though the world may be frigid and dim, Phainon and Mydei press on, the glint of gold on their fingers shining their way forward.
